description: The START menu's third page (interface/mod_settings/mod_settings.py). Each name below is a key of menu_texts: the text, in the game's five languages.

line.description: The first row of the third page and the description shown while the cursor is on it. The page's other rows are the game's "- - - - -" line.

entries.description: The small list that Mod Settings opens, in order, 1 to 10 rows, the most important first (in each list too, and a feature's on/off row first in its own list) (the game's small list shows 5: a list of more has a second page, and the pager at pager_place says which). A row has its name and its description and what A opens: another small list ({"entries": [rows]}, whose B comes back to this row), a screen of the code ({"title": a text, "screen": aspect_list}), or an option's list of values ({"option": key} alone: its name, description and title come from `options`). A row with "aspect" is left out unless the aspect ratio's switch is on, one with "wheel" unless the mod has the item wheel, and a row with "wheel_help" takes that description when the mod has it; an option the player's game cannot have is left out, and so is a list left with no row. All the lists together may have 10 lists and 64 rows (the code's data block, mod_settings.py MAX_LISTS and MAX_TABLE).

pager_place.description: Where a list's page number goes (a big list's, and a small list's of two pages, which then stands in for the menu's own), x and y in the top screen's layout: the place the game gives its own big lists.

ten_row_raise.description: In single-screen mode, how many pixels up a small list of ten rows goes from its place beside the page's first row, so that its tenth row stays clear of the description's place at the bottom left (the list from y 34 to 222, the place from y 196.25: 2 pixels apart). A shorter list goes 18 pixels a row less, none once its last row is clear (mod_settings.py list_raises), and every page of a list as far as its first. The list goes no higher than the screen's top (y 6). 0 to 255.

save_zone.description: Where a character keeps the mod's choices: 48 bytes at this offset of the save data (0x124E0; the data starts 0x5C into the save object and the file holds its first 0x12600 bytes), which no code of the game reads. A character without the magic has none yet. The aspect ratio is its byte 9, the options half a byte each in bytes 10 to 35 (`options`: option n in the low half of byte 10 + n / 2 for an even n, the high half for an odd one; room for 52), the item wheel's bytes 6 and 7 (its position and size, the low and high halves of byte 6; on or off, Auto-Combine and the trigger in byte 7) and 37 to 47 (its eight slots' items, 11 bits each; interface/radial_menu/radial_wheel.c); bytes 8 and 36 are unused. The choices count only in a zone with the magic and this version: an older zone (version 1 had no wheel, version 2 a byte per option) holds no choice, and the first choice of any kind makes it anew (zeros, the magic, the version).

menu_texts.description: The lines and descriptions of the menu, in the five languages, appended to each language's Menu file: the game finds a text by its index, the file's message count plus its place here, so a new text goes at the end. {slot} is filled by the code, in a row with the ratio's name. A row holds one line of text; a description (a key ending in _help) up to two, split by a line break as the game's own.

options.description: The options a player changes in the game, in the order of the code's option numbers (mod_options.py OPTION_IDS). title, when there is one: the text over the big list, when the row's name is too wide for it. key: the Settings field whose installed value is the default of a character with no choice yet (gui_defaults.json); default: for an option of this page only (no Settings field, no installer choice, in every edition's mod), the `setting` a character with no choice yet gets; name, help: menu texts; values: each with its name text, `setting` (the Settings value it stands for; a number picks the nearest) and what it writes or hands to a hook: `words` (whole numbers) or `floats`, at most two. The first value is the game's own behaviour. The save zone's byte of an option is 10 plus its number.
